rules.statement: A status type interrupt must be a wired level-triggered signal directly from the hardware input signal, qualified only by INTR_ENABLE, asserted continuously while the input is asserted.
The wired interrupt must not deassert until the root cause of the hardware input signal is addressed.
Software cannot acknowledge a status type interrupt via INTR_STATE, which is read-only (ro) in this context.
prim_intr_hw parameterized with .IntrT("Status") can generate the correct hardware for status type interrupts.

rules.condition: SW cannot address the root cause or wishes to defer handling
rules.statement: Software should mask the interrupt, at the peripheral or further up the tree such as the PLIC.

rules.condition: Masking a status interrupt at the peripheral
rules.statement: Software can mask at the peripheral by clearing the corresponding bit in INTR_ENABLE.
The block diagram shows one possible hardware implementation of an interrupt; other implementations are allowed.
The event sets the associated bit in INTR_STATE to 1.

rules.condition: Write of 1 to foo bit of INTR_TEST
rules.statement: A write of 1 to the foo bit of INTR_TEST can set the corresponding INTR_STATE bit.
The outgoing interrupt must be INTR_STATE ANDed with INTR_ENABLE.
A write of 1 to an INTR_STATE bit clears the latched value, but if the event is still active the bit returns to true.
Hardware must not clear the latched interrupt state; only software can.
Each peripheral can send zero or more alerts, each a distinguishable security threat.
Each alert originates in an internal event and must be handled within the peripheral and then within the alert handler module.
A recoverable alert sender must transmit one single alert event when the error condition is asserted.
A fatal alert sender must continuously transmit alert events until the system is reset.
Fatal alerts should also trigger local security countermeasures.
Error conditions should use the recommended alert type from the table; regular IRQ is optional.
A peripheral may optionally send a regular IRQ for any alert event.
Alerts shall be given a meaningful name indicative of their cause.
Recoverable alerts must be prefixed recov_ and fatal alerts must be prefixed fatal_.

rules.condition: Many diverse sources bundled into one alert
rules.statement: Alert names may default to just recov and/or fatal, implying only one alert of that type is exposed.
Each peripheral has a write-only ALERT_TEST register for software to test alert reporting.
Each alert has one field bit in ALERT_TEST, connected to the test input of the corresponding prim_alert_sender.
Internal events are sent active-high to the prim_alert_sender within the peripheral.
One prim_alert_sender must be instantiated per distinct alert event, with IsFatal set to 1 for fatal alerts.
The peripheral maintainer determines distinct alert events; multiple may be bundled.
Each peripheral should bundle alert sources into one or two distinct alerts, e.g. one fatal and one recoverable.
Comportable IPs with multiple bundled alerts should expose a cause register for disambiguation.
Recoverable alert cause registers must be clearable by SW or automatically cleared by HW.
Fatal alert cause registers must not be clearable and must be read-only.
The prim_alert_sender converts the event into a differentially encoded signal pair for the alert handler.
